name: Paparoa Track
why: Up a gold miners' track onto the tops of the Paparoa Range, a night at Moonlight Tops Hut above the Tasman Sea, then down through limestone and nīkau palms in the Pororari River gorge.
book: Ces Clark, Moonlight Tops and Pororari huts must be booked; there are no campsites. The start, Smoke-ho car park, is at the end of Blackball Road, 8 km north of Blackball (no camping there); shuttles serve both ends. Mountain bikers share the track.
water: Huts have a water supply, untreated: boil it before drinking.
dangers: About 6,000 mm of rain a year; heavy rain, snow, ice, fog and strong wind are possible on the exposed tops at any time.
The Pororari valley can become impassable in very heavy rain, with landslide and treefall risk: wait at Pororari Hut.
Mountain bikers use the same track: stay alert, especially on descents.
Cars have been broken into at the Smoke-ho, Waikori Road and Pororari car parks.
turnaround: If the weather becomes severe on the tops, stay in the hut or turn back to the last one until it improves (DOC).

points.name: Smoke-ho car park
points.note: End of Blackball Road. The rough historic Croesus Track climbs through podocarp and beech forest.

points.name: Ces Clark Hut
points.note: On the bushline after 10.3 km, past the historic Croesus Top Hut; on a clear day views to Lake Brunner and Aoraki.

points.name: Moonlight Tops Hut
points.note: First night after 20 km, most of the last part along the open ridge; sunsets over the Tasman Sea.

points.name: Pororari Hut
points.note: Second night after 19.1 km along the escarpment and down through ancient forest; the Lone Hand rock is across the valley.

points.name: Pororari River gorge
points.note: The track sidles the limestone gorge among beech, northern rātā and nīkau palms.

points.name: Pororari River car park, Punakaiki
points.note: On SH6, 1.2 km north of the Pancake Rocks.
